segments: ... and swallowed {OCR?} ... kings ... the sword.
And afterwards they were found with their blood shed upon their faces.
And many of the mothers gathered their children like a hen her brood,
and were waiting
either to die together by the sword,
or to be led away into captivity together.
And those who fled to the citadel,
the guards would not open to them,
until, they said, they saw the face of Joscelin {Papios}.
And when he did not hasten to come with the first,
thousands were crushed in the press.
And when he came,
he was unable to enter because of the heaps of corpses in front of the citadel gate.
And there he was struck by an arrow from the Turks and died.
And when Zengi saw the calamity,
he stayed the sword.
Then the bishop Basil was found, naked and barefoot,
and being dragged along with a rope by the Turks.
And when Zengi saw him,
he recognized the grace upon his face,
and asked, "Who is he?" And when he learned that he was the metropolitan,
he commanded, and they clothed him,
and brought him into his pavilion.
And he began to blame him for not having surrendered the city,
and spared the oppressed people from slaughter.
The bishop, however, replied,
"Divine Providence willed this,
so that you might have such a victory {OCR?},
and a great name and renown among the kings, your peers;
and that we, the wretched, might have boldness of face toward our Lord,
in that we were not deceitful, nor did we violate our oaths."
And his words pleased the Atabeg,
and he said to him:
"You have spoken the truth,
O Metropolitan.
For before God and before men, they are honorable who keep their oaths,
especially those who endure even unto death."
Now those who were in the citadel,
after two days, received a promise for their lives and surrendered it.
The Turks,
wherever they found a Frank, killed him,
but our people and the Armenians who were left, they spared.
Now the narration of this stroke does not belong to us to recount,
but rather to the prophet Jeremiah and to those like him,
who would call for the mourning women and the skilled women to compose laments with dirges and mournful thoughts over the pitiful people.
On that very day that Edessa was taken,
a fire broke out in the Monastery of Qararit in the region of Karshena,
and burned down all the cells, and one old monk;
and the rest escaped as if from a fiery furnace.
And on that day also, a village in the region of Marash burned down.
